site.risk.aria1: Where returns come from, and the risks
site.risk.3: Where returns come from, where the risk stays.
site.risk.5: 01Interest on the yield holdingRealised profit earns interest once it moves into a yield-bearing stablecoin. The rate floats and can fall.
site.risk.6: 02Taking profit and re-opening in volatile marketsEvery time one side is closed, read it together with the other side's unrealised loss. Realised alone overstates returns.
site.risk.8: 01Violent moves and liquidationBoth sides use margin. In violent markets or with too little margin, positions can still be liquidated.
site.risk.9: 02Funding ratesPerpetuals pay or charge funding on a schedule. Holding for long periods can keep eating into returns.
site.risk.10: 03Execution gapsSlippage, latency and exchange outages can all move fills away from the expected price.
site.risk.11: 04Rates and platformsYield rates change, and stablecoins and exchanges carry their own risks.
site.risk.12: Look at net value, not just realised
site.risk.13: Net valuewhat you really have=Wallet balanceprincipal and realised+Long unrealised P&Lopen, moves with price+Short unrealised P&Loften negative+Yield holdingfloating rate−Fees and fundingcharged while positions are open
site.risk.14: Judge returns by net value, not only by what's realised. Futures trading can lose money, and losses can be larger than expected.
site.tradeoff.2: You have 100 points. How would you split them?
site.tradeoff.3: Low risk, high return, cash any time: one pot of money rarely maxes out all three. Drag any slider and the other two give up points in proportion, so the total always stays at 100.
site.tradeoff.6: We don't claim all three. Here's which way the design leans.
site.tradeoff.7: RiskA long and a short at the same price reduce one-way price risk. Liquidation, funding and execution risk remain.
site.tradeoff.8: ReturnWhen one side takes profit, it moves into the yield holding. Rates change with the market; no fixed return is promised.
site.tradeoff.9: AccessFunds always stay in your own Binance account, and the platform can't withdraw. Positions must be closed before you take money out.
site.tradeoff.10: These points only explain a design trade-off. They are not a quantitative rating, a risk grade or a return guarantee.
site.tradeoff.14: Earns more, usually by taking on more
site.tradeoff.16: Money you can take out the moment you need it
site.tradeoff.18: Illustration · points show a trade-off only, not a rating · not investment advice
site.tradeoff.d.risk: Like term deposits or short-term bonds: small swings, usually modest returns, and some charge you for taking money out early.
site.tradeoff.d.yield: Like holding one-way spot or using leverage: big upside, and drawdowns that can run deep.
site.tradeoff.d.cash: Like a current account or money-market fund: available any time, usually the lowest return.
site.tradeoff.d.even: Wanting all three usually means getting only part of each.
site.tradeoff.d.noYield: Like a flexible savings product: steady and available any time, at the cost of limited returns.
site.tradeoff.d.noCash: Like fixed-term or locked savings: you give up access for a while in exchange for steadier returns.
site.tradeoff.d.noRisk: Like trading spot or futures yourself: you can sell any time and chase returns, but you carry the price swings.
site.tradeoff.d.me: Mostly on reducing one-way risk, then on return. Positions must be closed before you withdraw, so “cash any time” gets the fewest points.
site.safe.aria1: Fund safety design: sub-account API, withdrawals off, trading-pair whitelist
site.safe.3: Your money stays in your account. We only get permission to trade.
site.safe.4: We connect through the API of your Binance sub-account, and withdrawals must be switched off. This page never asks for a key and is not connected to any account.
site.safe.5: A sub-account, just for thisMove in only the funds you want to use for this strategy. Both accounts are in your name.
site.safe.6: API with read and futures trading onlyYou create and keep the key on Binance. Withdrawals and transfers out of the sub-account must be off.
site.safe.7: Withdrawals on? We won't connect.Permissions are checked at connection and while running. If anything goes beyond scope, we stop and tell you.
site.safe.8: A whitelist of up to 50 pairsOrders only go to the pairs you tick. The whitelist limits scope, not profit or loss.
site.safe.9: No withdrawals ≠ no risk. Trading permission alone can still lose money. To take funds back, close positions first, then transfer them yourself on Binance.

site.join.26: Always in your own Binance sub-account. We only place orders through that sub-account's API; funds never move to 3dtrading.
site.join.27: If I hold a long and a short, is there no risk?
site.join.28: No. Hedging reduces one-way price risk; liquidation, funding, slippage and execution gaps, rate changes and exchange risk all remain, and losses can be larger than expected.
site.join.29: With withdrawals and transfers off, am I safe?
site.join.30: The platform can't withdraw or move your funds, but it can still trade, and futures trading itself can lose money.
site.join.31: How do I take my money back?
site.join.32: Close every position in the sub-account first, then transfer the funds from the sub-account to your main account yourself on Binance. The API has no transfer or withdrawal permission, so only you can do this step.
site.join.33: Does this page collect my API key?
site.join.34: No. This is a local demo page with no input fields, and it doesn't connect to Binance or any server.
